import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source4_78_1 and Source4_78_0 on name == school
# Rename Source0.school to 'name' to join on same column name
source0_renamed = source0.rename(columns={"school": "name"})
join_1 = pd.merge(source1, source0_renamed, on="name", how="inner")

# Step 2: Join Source4_78_2 and Source4_78_0 on school == school
# This join is not directly used in final aggregation, but operation history shows it was done.
# We do not need to use this join for final output as per operation history and final aggregation.
# So we skip using this join in final output.

# Step 3: Group by and aggregate as specified:
# Group by Source4_78_1 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# Aggregations on Source4_78_0 columns:
# avg(Average Math Score), avg(Average Reading Score), sum(Number Passing Math), sum(Number Passing Reading)
# Also sum(Source4_78_1.size) as School Size (but size is already grouped by, so sum(size) = size)
# To avoid confusion, we will trust the operation history and use the join_1 dataframe for aggregation.

agg_df = join_1.groupby(
    ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget'],
    as_index=False
).agg({
    'Average Math Score': 'mean',
    'Average Reading Score': 'mean',
    'Number Passing Math': 'sum',
    'Number Passing Reading': 'sum',
    'size': 'sum'  # This will be renamed to 'School Size' later
})

# Rename 'size' sum to 'School Size'
agg_df = agg_df.rename(columns={'size': 'School Size'})

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['School ID': int, 'name': str, 'type': str, 'size': int, 'budget': int,
#  'Average Math Score': float, 'Average Reading Score': float,
#  'Number Passing Math': int, 'Number Passing Reading': int, 'School Size': int]

# 'size' column is from groupby key, so it is already present as 'size'
# Ensure correct types:
agg_df['School ID'] = agg_df['School ID'].astype(int)
agg_df['name'] = agg_df['name'].astype(str)
agg_df['type'] = agg_df['type'].astype(str)
agg_df['size'] = agg_df['size'].astype(int)
agg_df['budget'] = agg_df['budget'].astype(int)
agg_df['Average Math Score'] = agg_df['Average Math Score'].astype(float)
agg_df['Average Reading Score'] = agg_df['Average Reading Score'].astype(float)
agg_df['Number Passing Math'] = agg_df['Number Passing Math'].astype(int)
agg_df['Number Passing Reading'] = agg_df['Number Passing Reading'].astype(int)
agg_df['School Size'] = agg_df['School Size'].astype(int)

# Save to target path
agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source4_78_1 and Source4_78_0 on name=school
joined_1_0 = pd.merge(source1, source0, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")

# Group by the primary key columns from target schema: School ID, name, type, size, budget
# Aggregate Average Math Score and Average Reading Score by average
# Aggregate Number Passing Math and Number Passing Reading by sum
agg = joined_1_0.groupby(
    ["School ID", "name", "type", "size", "budget"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "Average Math Score": "mean",
    "Average Reading Score": "mean",
    "Number Passing Math": "sum",
    "Number Passing Reading": "sum"
})

# Join the aggregated result back with source1 on name to get School Size (size renamed as School Size)
# The target schema has a column "School Size" which equals "size" from source1
# So we join on name to bring size again as School Size
final = pd.merge(agg, source1[["name", "size"]], on="name", how="inner")

# Rename the last 'size' column to 'School Size' to match target schema
final = final.rename(columns={"size_y": "School Size", "size_x": "size"})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final = final[[
    "School ID", "name", "type", "size", "budget",
    "Average Math Score", "Average Reading Score",
    "Number Passing Math", "Number Passing Reading", "School Size"
]]

# Write output to the target file
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
